description: An eight-block sequencer that rewrites what it plays as you add and remove notes on its keyboard, with four note pools to switch between

params.text: Sets how many note blocks are played before the sequence returns to the first
Empties the current note pool and the sequence written from it
Makes its note pool the active one; pressing it again while it is already active writes a fresh random sequence from that pool
One beat of the sequence, holding up to four notes in one of nine subdivisions; left click to step forward, shift and left click to step back, right click to choose from a list
Sets the pitch of one note in the block: click for a keyboard carrying Rest, Tie and an Auto Advance button, or drag up and down to set the voltage

inputs.text: Advances the sequence one note block
Returns the sequence to its first note block when the voltage rises past 2V
Chooses the active note pool by voltage: 1V to a shade below 2V picks the first pool, and so on up to a shade below 5V for the fourth
Empties the current note pool and its sequence when the voltage rises past 2V

outputs.text: High while a note is playing, for the length set on the menu
The pitch of the note now playing
A gate at the end of each cycle

notes: nothing happens until a clock is patched; the module has no clock of its own
the sequence is written from the note pool, so it stays empty until notes are added on the keyboard strip
the keyboard strip is one drawing, not a row of controls: click a key to add or remove that note, drag up or down on it to set how often it appears, and no key can be clicked for help
this build has four note pools and reads 1V to a shade below 5V to select them; the maker's manual says eight pools
menu: Fill Remaining Sequence — fills every note block outside the current length at random, using the blocks that are inside it
Randomize All Note Pools — writes a fresh random pool into all four slots
Gate Length — sets how much of each note the gate output stays high for
Swing — delays every second note block
Clock Mode: Gate, Phase — reads the clock input either as a square wave, high above 2V and low below 0.1V, or as a ramp that advances a block when it falls from above 9V to below 1V
Randomize — randomises the pitches or the rhythm of the whole sequence
Shift & Shuffle — shifts and shuffles the sequence from the menu, the way the Shift & Shuffle expander does from its jacks
Set Rhythm — sets every note block to one subdivision
Note Pool — sets the pool of notes the randomisers draw from, from a scale, from a keyboard, or by shifting the current pool in semitones
Copy/Paste — copies and pastes the sequence or the note pool in a portable format that other JP sequencers read
Expanders — places an expander module beside this one

inputs.2:
unipolar · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
